basis: TechCrunch (2022-05-25): Zip's $43M Series B at a $1.2B valuation was led by YC Continuity with Tiger Global and CRV participating; TechCrunch (2023-05-16) has Tiger Global again in the $100M Series C. Private rounds naming the firm (T3); no vehicle named, so the home desk (D2)

note: Zip (ZipHQ), the San Francisco procurement software company founded 2020 by Rujul Zaparde and Lu Cheng. The prefilled status (acquired by Air Canada) and country (CA) came from a one-word Wikidata join to Zip, Air Canada's 2002-2004 low-cost airline, a different company; this Zip is private and operating (Zip Forward conference Sept 2026) and TechCrunch places its headquarters in San Francisco. Entry: Tiger first appears in the May 2022 $43M Series B at $1.2B (YC Continuity led; Tiger Global and CRV participated). The earlier $25M Series A named no investors in any source checked (TechCrunch 2022 and 2023, Pulse 2.0, one web search, Tracxn read as a lead only), so the entry reads Growth at medium confidence. Mark: $190M Series D at $2.2B led by BOND (2024-10-21, SiliconANGLE), matching the YC book's $2.2B. Momentum check 2026-09-29 (Bing News): no later priced round.

Zipline, the South San Francisco drone delivery company. Tiger entered in the January 2026 $600M round at $7.6B: TechCrunch names 'several existing and new investors, including Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Valor Equity Partners, and Tiger Global'; no earlier Zipline round names Tiger. Growth by any reading (the company's Series A was a decade earlier). Mark $7.6B (Reuters 2026-01-20), the same as the a16z, Felicis and Sequoia books; a $200M extension followed in March 2026. Bloomberg reported talks in Sept 2026 to raise about $1B at about $20B: talks, not a closed round, so not a mark. The unicorn-list flags are cleared by this cited mark.

Zippi, the São Paulo fintech giving weekly credit to self-employed workers (a Y Combinator company). Tiger led the $16M Series A in June 2022 (LatamList; Estadão lists Y Combinator, Volpe Capital, Rainfall and others following), its first round in the company. Still operating: FIDC credit-fund raises in Sept 2025 and Feb 2026 (R$220M, with Credit Saison entering). Momentum check 2026-09-29 (Bing News): no equity round since the Series A, none at $1B or more.

basis: ZKH's IPO draft registration (2022-03-30) principal-shareholder table: 249,348,600 Series C-1 and 29,194,100 Series E preferred held by Internet Fund IV Pte. Ltd., a Singapore vehicle advised by Tiger Global Management (a private-investment vehicle, D2/D8); Tiger partner Pengfei Wang a director of ZKH Industrial Supply since June 2018. A private-round position, not a listed-stock purchase (T3); the 2024 13G and 13F lines are the later public holding

note: ZKH Group (震坤行), the Shanghai MRO industrial-supply procurement platform; principal executive offices in Minhang District, Shanghai per the filing. Tiger's vehicle Internet Fund IV holds Series C-1 (its first series; the filing's 2021-12-30 issuance dates are the offshore restructuring's mirror shares) and bought $5M more Series E on 2022-02-24. The onshore Series C is dated to 2018 by Tiger partner Pengfei Wang's seat on ZKH Industrial Supply's board from June 2018; no press report of that round was found (Bing and Google News, English and Chinese). Listed on the NYSE in Dec 2023; market cap $439.41M on 2026-09-29 (stockanalysis.com).

ZO Rooms was the budget-hotel brand of Zostel Hospitality Pvt Ltd, which also runs the Zostel hostels. VCCircle (2015-07-20): 'a fresh Series A round of funding led by Tiger Global with participation from Orios Venture Partners' (talks in May 2015 were for $10-15M). Status: OYO signed a term sheet in Nov 2015 to buy the ZO Rooms business for about 7% of OYO, took over its hotels and staff, and never issued the shares; the 2021 arbitral award for Zostel was set aside by the Delhi High Court in May 2025 and the Supreme Court dismissed Zostel's petition in July 2025 (appeal still listed in 2026). No acquisition closed, and the company Tiger funded still operates (Zostel hostels and Zo Houses; new property June 2026), so it reads private. City: 'the Delhi-based company' in a 2015 profile (breathedreamgo); no newer head-office statement found.

Zomato, now Eternal Ltd, the Gurugram food-delivery and quick-commerce company. Tiger's first check was about $103M (Rs 760 crore) in Sept 2020 (HT Tech; Techcircle had reported the planned raise in Aug 2020), part of the $660M Series J at $3.9B that closed in Jan 2021 (Pulse 2.0 names Tiger Global); it joined the Feb 2021 $250M round at $5.4B (Wikipedia). The vehicle was Internet Fund III Pte Ltd, a Tiger private-investment vehicle, which sold down in 2022 and exited in Aug 2023 (Mint). Listed July 2021. Market cap INR 3.04 trillion on 2026-09-29 (stockanalysis.com): INR 3040.00B @ ECB 2026-09-29 (INR/EUR 108.991, EUR/USD 1.1355) = $31.67B. Country IN confirmed from the company's own record (the prefill was a one-word name join).

Zopper, formerly Reviews42 (Solvy Tech Solutions), now a Noida insurtech platform. Reviews42 raised a seed from Blume Ventures and VentureEast (2012) and a Series A led by Nirvana Venture Advisors (2013) without Tiger; Tiger entered in the July 2014 $5M Series B with Nirvana (ETRetail), then led a $20M round in June 2015. PhonePe bought only the Zopper Retail point-of-sale unit in July 2018; the company continued and raised a $75M Series C (Creaegis, 2022) and a $25M Series D (Elevation, Dharana, Nov 2024); it targets an IPO around 2028-29. No $1B mark (about $125M raised in total by 2025).

Zovi (Robemall Apparels), the Bangalore private-label fashion e-tailer. VCCircle (2012-05-31): a $10M Series B 'from Tiger Global besides existing investor' SAIF Partners, so Tiger's first round was the B. SAIF and Tiger put in $10M more when Zovi took over Inkfruit (Feb 2013). In July 2015 the founders raised $50M from Paytm, SAIF and Tiger for a new deals app, Little (a separate venture, not this row). The Zovi store was reported out of order and near closure in Aug 2016 (Economic Times; YourStory) with no buyer named: defunct.

Zowie, the AI customer-service agent platform founded 2019 by Maja Schaefer and Matt Ciolek. Tiger led the $14M Series A in May 2022 (Business Insider; the company's release) after a $5M seed led by Gradient Ventures and 10xFounders in Jan 2022 without Tiger (TechCrunch). Place: the release says it 'operates between its commercial office in New York with development offices across Poland' (dateline New York), read as a New York head office with Polish engineering. Still operating (listed among enterprise AI voice-agent platforms, Sept 2026). Momentum check 2026-09-29 (Bing News): no later priced round found, none at $1B or more.

Zuoyebang, the Beijing online tutoring company spun out of Baidu in 2015. Tiger's first round is the June 2020 $750M Series E it co-led with FountainVest (TechNode). The model-memory lead that Tiger co-led a 2018 round did not hold: Reuters' June 2020 investor list (Goldman Sachs, Sequoia China, Coatue, GGV) omits Tiger, and the Coatue book records Coatue leading the July 2018 $350M Series D. Tiger joined the Dec 2020 $1.6B Series E+ at $9.6B post-money (equalocean names Tiger), the last priced round and the Coatue book's mark. China's July 2021 after-school tutoring rules hit the sector, but no priced round, tender or sale since was found (Bing News 2026-09-29), so the last primary stands, stale-flagged.

basis: Zynga's Fifth Amended and Restated Investors' Rights Agreement (dated 2011-02-18, filed as an exhibit to the IPO S-1/A 2011-08-11) lists Tiger Global Private Investment Partners V, L.P. (a PIP vehicle, the home desk) among the investors, with 554,362 registrable shares: a position in the private company before the Dec 2011 IPO (T3, D6). The 2012-2013 13G filings and 2013-2014 13F listings are the later public holding, not the entry

note: Zynga, the San Francisco social-games company, bought by Take-Two Interactive (closed May 2022). The rights agreement signed at the Feb 2011 Series C closing lists Tiger PIP V as a holder, but the S-1/A names Tiger in no issuance (the $490M Series C went to five new investors and one existing one) and records heavy secondary trading from late 2009; so Tiger entered either in the Series C or by a secondary purchase in 2010-2011. Either reads Growth (the company had closed its Series A to B-2 by 2010, at a $4.25B valuation in April 2010). The entry date is the agreement's year, the earliest dated record of the position.
